verdict.rationale: Elasticsearch's `semantic_text` field automatically generates embeddings at index time using a configured model. The docs say you only create a mapping to start "ingesting, embedding, and querying", with no inference ingest pipelines needed. Models can also be deployed directly in Elasticsearch or used as hosted/external models. missing for 10: explicit documentation that query text is vectorized automatically at search time (only implied), detail on which built-in or Elastic-managed embedding models are available, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use built-in or managed embedders so documents and queries are vectorized without running my own embedding pipeline

citations.quote: When you index content into a `semantic_text` field, Elasticsearch automatically generates vector embeddings using a configured machine learning model and stores them in the underlying vector field.

All you need to do is create an index mapping to start ingesting, embedding, and querying data. There is no need to define model-related settings and parameters, or to create inference ingest pipelines.
Option 3: Deploy models directly in Elasticsearch
You can deploy external or hosted embedding models, or bring your own pre-computed vectors.
